## Magnetic Letters Hero (`hero-magnetic-letters`)

Dark editorial hero where every letter of the headline tracks the cursor under its own spring physics. Configurable pull radius and strength. The backdrop is three large blurred gradient orbs (teal, magenta, amber) drifting diagonally on independent slow loops with `mix-blend: screen`, layered with a static SVG-turbulence film grain. A soft white glow fades in around letters as the pointer approaches.

- Docs: https://uniqueui-platform.vercel.app/blocks/hero-magnetic-letters
- Install: `npx uniqueui add hero-magnetic-letters`
- shadcn CLI: `npx shadcn@latest add https://uniqueui-platform.vercel.app/r/hero-magnetic-letters.json`
- Category: Hero
- Tags: hero, block, text, magnetic
- Peer dependencies: react, react-dom

Per-glyph cursor-tracking hero. The headline reads as a normal h1 to screen readers (aria-label on the wrapper, aria-hidden on each animated span), so accessibility is preserved despite the per-letter wrapping.

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | Override the entire hero composition (eyebrow + headline + sub + CTAs). When omitted, a default composition renders that uses the `headline` prop. |
| `headline` | `string` | `"Motion, where it matters."` | Headline text. Each glyph becomes an independent motion target — set this instead of passing `children` if you only want to swap copy. |
| `radius` | `number` | `160` | Pixel radius around each letter within which the cursor exerts pull. Outside the radius the letter rests at its natural position. |
| `strength` | `number` | `14` | Maximum displacement (in px) any single letter can reach at peak proximity to the cursor. |
| `className` | `string` | — | Extra classes on the outer `<section>`. |

### Usage

```tsx
import { MagneticLettersHero } from "@/components/ui/hero-magnetic-letters";

export default function Hero() {
  return <MagneticLettersHero headline="Motion, where it matters." />;
}
```

## Terminal Hero (`hero-terminal`)

A 'code-builds-the-page' hero: a headline above a macOS-style terminal that types your install commands and prints their output. Ships the reusable Terminal window too, with reduced-motion, in-view triggering, replay, copy, and keystroke sound.

- Docs: https://uniqueui-platform.vercel.app/blocks/hero-terminal
- Install: `npx uniqueui add hero-terminal`
- shadcn CLI: `npx shadcn@latest add https://uniqueui-platform.vercel.app/r/hero-terminal.json`
- Category: Hero
- Tags: terminal, cli, typing, code, hero
- Peer dependencies: react, react-dom

TerminalHero pairs a headline with a live terminal that types your getting-started commands and prints their output — a high-conversion 'see it work' pattern for landing pages. The standalone `Terminal` window is exported from the same file for reuse elsewhere. The animation starts when the hero scrolls into view, respects `prefers-reduced-motion` (rendering the finished transcript instantly), and exposes copy + replay controls. The animated transcript is `aria-hidden` while a screen-reader-only copy carries the real content.

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | Slotted hero content above the terminal (headline / subhead / CTAs). When omitted, a default composition renders. |
| `commands` | `string[]` | — | Commands typed out sequentially in the terminal. Defaults to a shadcn init/install sequence. |
| `outputs` | `Record<number, string[]>` | `{}` | Output lines printed after a command finishes typing, keyed by the command's index. |
| `username` | `string` | `"you"` | Name shown highlighted in the shell prompt (renders as `username:~$`). |
| `title` | `string` | `"zsh — your-project"` | Text shown centered in the window title bar. |
| `typingSpeed` | `number` | `50` | Typing speed in milliseconds per character. |
| `delayBetweenCommands` | `number` | `800` | Pause in milliseconds after a command's output before the next command starts. |
| `initialDelay` | `number` | `500` | Delay in milliseconds before the first command begins typing. |
| `enableSound` | `boolean` | `false` | Play a subtle keystroke click on each character via the Web Audio API. Defaults off in the hero to avoid autoplay audio. |
| `loop` | `boolean` | `false` | Restart the typing sequence from the top once it finishes. |
| `className` | `string` | — | Extra classes on the outer `<section>`. |

### Usage

```tsx
import { TerminalHero } from "@/components/ui/hero-terminal";

export default function Hero() {
  return (
    <TerminalHero
      username="you"
      title="zsh — your-project"
      commands={[
        "npx shadcn@latest init",
        "npm install motion",
        "npx shadcn@latest add button card",
      ]}
      outputs={{
        0: [
          "✔ Preflight checks passed.",
          "✔ Created components.json",
          "✔ Initialized project.",
        ],
        1: ["added 1 package in 2s"],
        2: ["✔ Done. Installed button, card."],
      }}
    >
      <span className="mb-5 inline-flex items-center gap-2 rounded-full border border-white/15 bg-white/5 px-3 py-1 text-xs uppercase tracking-[0.18em] text-white/70 backdrop-blur">
        One command to ship
      </span>
      <h1 className="text-balance text-4xl font-semibold tracking-tight sm:text-6xl">
        Watch your stack build itself.
      </h1>
      <p className="mt-5 max-w-xl text-pretty text-base text-white/65 sm:text-lg">
        Copy-paste components, zero config — production-ready before the cursor
        stops blinking.
      </p>
    </TerminalHero>
  );
}
```

## Flow Field Hero (`hero-flow-field`)

A canvas-rendered hero block. Particles advect along a summed-sine flow field, leaving comet trails that bend and wave as you scroll — the field's phase is driven by `window.scrollY`. Scroll-driven (not cursor-driven), with light/dark `theme` support, a centered scrim that keeps headline text legible over the field, devicePixelRatio-aware rendering, a static `prefers-reduced-motion` fallback, and zero external animation deps beyond `motion`.

- Docs: https://uniqueui-platform.vercel.app/blocks/hero-flow-field
- Install: `npx uniqueui add hero-flow-field`
- shadcn CLI: `npx shadcn@latest add https://uniqueui-platform.vercel.app/r/hero-flow-field.json`
- Category: Hero
- Tags: hero, block, canvas, streamlines, field
- Peer dependencies: react, react-dom

Scroll-driven canvas flow field. Particles flow along a summed-sine vector field and leave fading comet trails; the field's phase tracks `window.scrollY`, so the streamlines bend and wave as the page scrolls, with a slow idle drift keeping it alive at rest. A centered radial scrim lifts text contrast over the field, and the `theme` prop switches the whole palette (field, scrim, text, CTAs) between light and dark. `FlowFieldBackground` is a separate export and can be reused under any composition.

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `theme` | `"light" \| "dark"` | `"dark"` | Palette for the field, scrim, text, and CTAs. Forwarded to the background and default content. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | Slotted hero content. Omit for the default theme-aware headline + CTAs. |
| `className` | `string` | — | Classes for the outer `<section>`. |
| `backgroundProps` | `{ theme?: "light" \| "dark"; colors?: [string, string]; density?: number; lineWidth?: number; scrollStrength?: number; speed?: number; trail?: number; className?: string }` | — | Forwarded to the canvas background layer (`FlowFieldBackground`). `density` scales particle count (0.2–3); `trail` sets comet-tail length (0.8–0.98); `scrollStrength` controls how hard scroll bends the field. |

### Usage

```tsx
import { FlowFieldHero } from "@/components/ui/hero-flow-field";

export default function Hero() {
  return (
    <FlowFieldHero theme="dark">
      <span className="mb-5 inline-flex items-center gap-2 rounded-full border border-white/15 bg-white/5 px-3 py-1 font-mono text-[10px] uppercase tracking-[0.2em] text-white/70 backdrop-blur">
        <span
          aria-hidden
          className="h-1.5 w-1.5 rounded-full bg-sky-400 shadow-[0_0_10px_2px] shadow-sky-400/40"
        />
        Field · scroll to flow
      </span>
      <h1 className="text-balance text-4xl font-semibold tracking-tight sm:text-6xl">
        Momentum you can see.
      </h1>
      <p className="mt-5 max-w-xl text-pretty text-base text-white/65 sm:text-lg">
        A canvas flow field of streamlines that bend and wave with the page
        scroll position. Scroll-driven, not cursor-driven — no external deps.
      </p>
      <div className="mt-9 flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-3">
        <button
          type="button"
          className="group inline-flex h-11 cursor-pointer items-center gap-2 rounded-full bg-white px-6 text-sm font-medium text-black transition-transform duration-200 hover:-translate-y-px"
        >
          <span>Get started</span>
          <span aria-hidden className="transition-transform duration-200 group-hover:translate-x-0.5">
            →
          </span>
        </button>
        <button
          type="button"
          className="inline-flex h-11 cursor-pointer items-center gap-2 rounded-full border border-white/15 px-6 font-mono text-xs uppercase tracking-[0.18em] text-white/85 backdrop-blur transition-colors hover:bg-white/5"
        >
          View source
        </button>
      </div>
    </FlowFieldHero>
  );
}
```

## Radial Burst Hero (`hero-radial-burst`)

A Stripe-style hero block: an interactive fiber-optic radial burst on canvas. Fine glowing rays stream out of a bottom-center origin in a wide fan, each one continuously growing, over-extending, fading, and regenerating with fresh angle/length/speed/opacity, with a single glowing dot riding each fiber's tip. Hovering the middle or tip of a fiber makes it (and its neighbours) brighten, stretch, and bend toward the cursor, then ease back to their drift; the dense zone near the origin stays calm. The burst sits in a short lower band, masked so it fades out below the headline. Ships with six time-of-day themes (Pre-dawn, Sunrise, Daytime, Dusk, Sunset, Night) and an in-block switcher; the background crossfades and the burst colors lerp between themes. devicePixelRatio-aware, keyboard-accessible switcher, honors `prefers-reduced-motion` (renders a calm static frame), and uses `motion` for the intro, theme blend, and dropdown.

- Docs: https://uniqueui-platform.vercel.app/blocks/hero-radial-burst
- Install: `npx uniqueui add hero-radial-burst`
- shadcn CLI: `npx shadcn@latest add https://uniqueui-platform.vercel.app/r/hero-radial-burst.json`
- Category: Hero
- Tags: hero, block, canvas, starburst, interactive, particles
- Peer dependencies: react, react-dom

An interactive fiber-optic burst rises from a bottom-center origin that touches the bottom edge: fine rays fan across the upper semicircle (longest near vertical, forming a soft dome), each a base-bright→tip-faint gradient drawn as a soft wide glow pass plus a crisp core, with a single glowing dot riding its tip. Every ray continuously grows, slightly over-extends, fades, and respawns with a fresh angle, length, speed, and opacity, so the loop is seamless with no global reset. Hovering the middle or tip of a fiber makes it and its neighbours brighten, stretch, and bend toward the cursor before easing back; the dense zone near the origin does not react. The burst is kept to a short lower band, masked so it never reaches the headline above. Six time-of-day themes — Pre-dawn, Sunrise, Daytime, Dusk, Sunset, Night — are selectable from an in-block dropdown; switching crossfades the background gradient and eases the burst colors between palettes. `RadialBurst` is exported separately for reuse under your own layout.

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultTheme` | `"pre-dawn" \| "sunrise" \| "daytime" \| "dusk" \| "sunset" \| "night"` | `"night"` | Initial time-of-day theme. Re-synced if it changes (e.g. from a site theme toggle); the in-block switcher overrides until then. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | — | Headline content. Defaults to "The backbone of global commerce". |
| `burstProps` | `{ className?: string; density?: number; interactive?: boolean }` | — | Forwarded to the canvas burst layer (`RadialBurst`). `density` scales ray count (0.4–2); set `interactive` to false to disable pointer reactivity. |
| `className` | `string` | — | Classes for the outer `<section>`. |

### Usage

```tsx
import { RadialBurstHero } from "@/components/ui/hero-radial-burst";

export default function Hero() {
  return (
    <RadialBurstHero
      defaultTheme="night"
      title={
        <>
          The backbone
          <br />
          of global commerce
        </>
      }
    />
  );
}
```

## Animated Tooltip (`animated-tooltip`)

An accessible, spring-animated tooltip with a customizable pointing arrow. Background, text, and arrow colours are independently configurable, and it follows WAI-ARIA guidance — hover/focus triggers, role="tooltip", aria-describedby, and Escape to dismiss.

- Docs: https://uniqueui-platform.vercel.app/components/animated-tooltip
- Install: `npx uniqueui add animated-tooltip`
- shadcn CLI: `npx shadcn@latest add https://uniqueui-platform.vercel.app/r/animated-tooltip.json`
- Category: Navigation & Overlays
- Tags: overlay, tooltip, accessibility
- Peer dependencies: react, react-dom

AnimatedTooltip wraps any single focusable element and shows a floating label on hover and keyboard focus. It follows the WAI-ARIA tooltip pattern: the bubble carries role="tooltip", the trigger is linked via aria-describedby while open, and pressing Escape dismisses it. The bubble and its pointing arrow are styled through independent props, so you can recolour the background, the text, and the arrow separately. Enter/exit uses a spring and automatically falls back to a plain fade when the user prefers reduced motion.

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `React.ReactElement` | — | The trigger element. Must be a single focusable React element (e.g. a button or link). |
| `content` | `React.ReactNode` | — | Content rendered inside the tooltip bubble. |
| `side` | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right"` | `"top"` | Which side of the trigger the tooltip appears on. |
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | `"center"` | Alignment along the trigger's edge. |
| `background` | `string` | `"#18181b"` | Background colour of the tooltip bubble. |
| `color` | `string` | `"#fafafa"` | Text colour inside the tooltip. |
| `arrowColor` | `string` | — | Arrow fill colour. Defaults to `background` so it always matches. |
| `arrow` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether to render the pointing arrow. |
| `arrowSize` | `number` | `8` | Arrow edge length in px. |
| `offset` | `number` | `8` | Gap between the trigger and the tooltip in px. |
| `delay` | `number` | `200` | Delay before the tooltip appears, in ms. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disable the tooltip entirely (the trigger still renders). |
| `className` | `string` | — | Extra Tailwind classes merged onto the tooltip bubble. |

### Usage

```tsx
"use client";
import { AnimatedTooltip } from "@/components/ui/animated-tooltip";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <AnimatedTooltip content="Copy to clipboard" side="top">
      <button className="rounded-md bg-neutral-800 px-4 py-2 text-sm text-white">
        Copy
      </button>
    </AnimatedTooltip>
  );
}
```

### Scenario: Recolour background, text, and arrow independently

Set `background`, `color`, and `arrowColor` to fully theme the tooltip. The arrow defaults to the background colour but can be overridden for a contrasting tip.

```tsx
"use client";
import { AnimatedTooltip } from "@/components/ui/animated-tooltip";

export default function ThemedTooltip() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center justify-center gap-6 p-16">
      <AnimatedTooltip
        content="Brand-coloured tooltip"
        background="#7c3aed"
        color="#ffffff"
        arrowColor="#7c3aed"
      >
        <button className="rounded-md bg-violet-600 px-4 py-2 text-sm text-white">
          Hover me
        </button>
      </AnimatedTooltip>

      <AnimatedTooltip
        content="Contrasting arrow tip"
        background="#f59e0b"
        color="#1c1917"
        arrowColor="#ef4444"
      >
        <button className="rounded-md bg-amber-500 px-4 py-2 text-sm text-neutral-900">
          Mismatched arrow
        </button>
      </AnimatedTooltip>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Scenario: Placement on any side

Use `side` and `align` to position the tooltip — the arrow tracks the chosen edge and alignment automatically.

```tsx
"use client";
import { AnimatedTooltip } from "@/components/ui/animated-tooltip";

export default function PlacedTooltips() {
  const btn = "rounded-md bg-neutral-800 px-4 py-2 text-sm text-white";
  return (
    <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-6 p-16">
      <AnimatedTooltip content="Top" side="top"><button className={btn}>Top</button></AnimatedTooltip>
      <AnimatedTooltip content="Right" side="right"><button className={btn}>Right</button></AnimatedTooltip>
      <AnimatedTooltip content="Bottom" side="bottom"><button className={btn}>Bottom</button></AnimatedTooltip>
      <AnimatedTooltip content="Left" side="left"><button className={btn}>Left</button></AnimatedTooltip>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Scenario: No arrow with a custom delay

Set `arrow={false}` for a flat label and tune `delay` to control how quickly it appears.

```tsx
"use client";
import { AnimatedTooltip } from "@/components/ui/animated-tooltip";

export default function MinimalTooltip() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center justify-center p-16">
      <AnimatedTooltip content="Instant, arrowless label" arrow={false} delay={0} offset={6}>
        <button className="rounded-md bg-neutral-800 px-4 py-2 text-sm text-white">
          Hover me
        </button>
      </AnimatedTooltip>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Scenario: Rich, multi-line content

`content` accepts any React node, so you can render a heading, body copy, or a keyboard shortcut. Use `className` to widen the bubble.

```tsx
"use client";
import { AnimatedTooltip } from "@/components/ui/animated-tooltip";

export default function RichTooltip() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center justify-center p-16">
      <AnimatedTooltip
        side="bottom"
        className="max-w-[16rem]"
        background="#0f172a"
        color="#e2e8f0"
        content={
          <div className="space-y-1">
            <p className="font-semibold">Keyboard shortcut</p>
            <p className="text-xs text-slate-400">
              Press {"\u2318"}K to open the command palette from anywhere.
            </p>
          </div>
        }
      >
        <button className="rounded-md bg-slate-800 px-4 py-2 text-sm text-white">
          Command palette
        </button>
      </AnimatedTooltip>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Scenario: Any trigger — icon buttons and links

The trigger can be any single focusable element. Hover and keyboard focus both work because the tooltip listens via bubbling focus events.

```tsx
"use client";
import { AnimatedTooltip } from "@/components/ui/animated-tooltip";
import { Info } from "lucide-react";

export default function TriggerVariants() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center justify-center gap-8 p-16">
      <AnimatedTooltip content="More information" side="top">
        <button
          aria-label="More information"
          className="grid h-9 w-9 place-items-center rounded-full bg-neutral-800 text-white"
        >
          <Info className="h-4 w-4" />
        </button>
      </AnimatedTooltip>

      <AnimatedTooltip content="Opens in a new tab" side="top">
        <a
          href="https://example.com"
          className="text-sm font-medium text-violet-500 underline underline-offset-4"
        >
          Documentation
        </a>
      </AnimatedTooltip>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Autocomplete Search (`autocomplete-search`)

Accessible combobox with debounced filtering, async-ready search, full keyboard navigation, grouped options, matched-text highlighting, and loading / empty / error states.

- Docs: https://uniqueui-platform.vercel.app/components/autocomplete-search
- Install: `npx uniqueui add autocomplete-search`
- shadcn CLI: `npx shadcn@latest add https://uniqueui-platform.vercel.app/r/autocomplete-search.json`
- Category: Components
- Tags: search, combobox, autocomplete, input, form
- Peer dependencies: react, react-dom, lucide-react

AutocompleteSearch is an accessible combobox following the W3C APG editable-combobox-with-list-autocomplete pattern. Pass a static `options` array for synchronous local filtering, or an async `onSearch` resolver for remote search — the latter debounces requests and guards against stale responses overwriting newer queries. Typing is debounced (300ms by default), the matched substring is highlighted in each result, and consecutive options sharing a `group` render as labelled sections. Keyboard support: ArrowUp/ArrowDown move the active option (wrapping), Enter selects, Escape closes then clears. It exposes combobox/listbox/option roles with aria-activedescendant and a polite live region, honors prefers-reduced-motion, and is SSR-safe.

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `AutocompleteOption[]` | — | Static option list for synchronous local filtering. Ignored when onSearch is provided. |
| `onSearch` | `(query: string) => Promise<AutocompleteOption[]>` | — | Async resolver returning matches for a query. Enables async mode with loading/error states and a stale-response guard. |
| `onSelect` | `(option: AutocompleteOption) => void` | — | Called when an option is chosen via click or Enter. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `"Search…"` | Input placeholder; also used as the combobox/listbox accessible name. |
| `debounceMs` | `number` | `300` | Delay before filtering (sync) or fetching (async) after the last keystroke. |
| `minChars` | `number` | `0` | Minimum characters before a search runs. Below this, results are cleared and hintMessage (if set) shows. |
| `emptyMessage` | `string` | `"No results found"` | Shown when a search completes with zero matches. |
| `loadingMessage` | `string` | `"Searching…"` | Shown in async mode while onSearch is pending. |
| `hintMessage` | `string` | — | Shown when the query length is below minChars. Only rendered if provided. |
| `errorMessage` | `string` | `"Something went wrong. Try again."` | Shown when onSearch rejects. |
| `theme` | `"light" \| "dark"` | `"dark"` | Theme for default input and dropdown colors. |
| `className` | `string` | — | Additional classes merged onto the root wrapper. |

### Usage

```tsx
"use client";
import {
  AutocompleteSearch,
  type AutocompleteOption,
} from "@/components/ui/autocomplete-search";

const frameworks: AutocompleteOption[] = [
  { value: "next", label: "Next.js" },
  { value: "remix", label: "Remix" },
  { value: "astro", label: "Astro" },
  { value: "svelte", label: "SvelteKit" },
  { value: "nuxt", label: "Nuxt" },
  { value: "solid", label: "SolidStart" },
  { value: "vite", label: "Vite" },
  { value: "gatsby", label: "Gatsby" },
];

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="flex h-[440px] w-full justify-center px-6 pt-10">
      <AutocompleteSearch
        options={frameworks}
        placeholder="Search frameworks…"
        theme="dark"
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Scenario: Filter a static list

Pass an options array for instant, debounced local filtering with matched-text highlighting — no network needed.

```tsx
"use client";
import {
  AutocompleteSearch,
  type AutocompleteOption,
} from "@/components/ui/autocomplete-search";

const frameworks: AutocompleteOption[] = [
  { value: "next", label: "Next.js" },
  { value: "remix", label: "Remix" },
  { value: "astro", label: "Astro" },
  { value: "svelte", label: "SvelteKit" },
  { value: "nuxt", label: "Nuxt" },
];

export default function FrameworkPicker() {
  return (
    <AutocompleteSearch
      options={frameworks}
      placeholder="Search frameworks…"
      onSelect={(o) => console.log("picked", o.value)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Scenario: Grouped command menu

Give options a `group` to render labelled sections (role="group"); keyboard navigation flows across groups seamlessly.

```tsx
"use client";
import {
  AutocompleteSearch,
  type AutocompleteOption,
} from "@/components/ui/autocomplete-search";

const commands: AutocompleteOption[] = [
  { value: "new-file", label: "New File", group: "Actions" },
  { value: "save-all", label: "Save All", group: "Actions" },
  { value: "profile", label: "Profile", group: "Account" },
  { value: "logout", label: "Log out", group: "Account" },
  { value: "docs", label: "Documentation", group: "Help" },
];

export default function CommandMenu() {
  return (
    <AutocompleteSearch options={commands} placeholder="Type a command…" />
  );
}
```

### Scenario: Async remote search

Provide onSearch to fetch results from an API. Requests are debounced and stale responses are discarded, with built-in loading, empty, and error states. Use minChars + hintMessage to defer searching until enough is typed.

```tsx
"use client";
import {
  AutocompleteSearch,
  type AutocompleteOption,
} from "@/components/ui/autocomplete-search";

async function searchUsers(query: string): Promise<AutocompleteOption[]> {
  const res = await fetch(`/api/users?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}`);
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error("request failed");
  const users = (await res.json()) as { id: string; name: string; email: string }[];
  return users.map((u) => ({ value: u.id, label: u.name, description: u.email }));
}

export default function UserSearch() {
  return (
    <AutocompleteSearch
      onSearch={searchUsers}
      minChars={2}
      placeholder="Search users…"
      hintMessage="Type at least 2 characters"
      emptyMessage="No users match that search"
    />
  );
}
```

## Dropdown (`dropdown`)

Animated single and multi select dropdown with search, select all / deselect all, removable chips, per-option icons, color dots, descriptions, disabled options, grouping, and checkbox / radio / check indicators. Fully keyboard accessible.

- Docs: https://uniqueui-platform.vercel.app/components/dropdown
- Install: `npx uniqueui add dropdown`
- shadcn CLI: `npx shadcn@latest add https://uniqueui-platform.vercel.app/r/dropdown.json`
- Category: Components
- Tags: dropdown, select, multiselect, form, input
- Peer dependencies: react, react-dom, lucide-react

Dropdown is a single- and multi-select control in one component. Set `multiple` to switch modes: single shows a check (or radio) on the chosen item; multiple shows checkbox indicators, a count or removable chips in the trigger, and an optional Select all / Deselect all row with an indeterminate state. Options support leading icons or color dots, secondary descriptions, disabled entries, and grouping (consecutive options sharing `group` render under a section header). `searchable` adds an in-panel filter, `clearable` adds a reset button. It is keyboard operable (Arrow keys, Enter/Space to toggle, Home/End, Escape, Tab) with combobox + listbox/option roles, aria-multiselectable, aria-activedescendant, and aria-selected/aria-disabled. The panel animates open with a spring and chips animate in/out; everything collapses to instant under prefers-reduced-motion. Works controlled (via `value`) or uncontrolled (via `defaultValue`).

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `DropdownOption[]` | — | Items: { value, label, icon?, color?, description?, group?, disabled? }. Consecutive options sharing a group render as a labelled section. |
| `value` | `string \| string[]` | — | Controlled value — string[] in multiple mode, string in single mode. Omit for uncontrolled. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| string[]` | — | Initial value when uncontrolled. |
| `onChange` | `(value: string \| string[]) => void` | — | Fires on selection change. Receives string[] when multiple, otherwise the selected string ("" when cleared). |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `false` | Enable multi-select (checkbox indicators, chips/count, select all). |
| `searchable` | `boolean` | `false` | Show an in-panel search box that filters options by label. |
| `clearable` | `boolean` | `false` | Show a clear (×) button in the trigger when there is a selection. |
| `showSelectAll` | `boolean` | `false` | Multiple mode: show a Select all / Deselect all row with an indeterminate state. |
| `selectionIndicator` | `"checkbox" \| "radio" \| "check" \| "none"` | — | Per-option marker. Defaults to checkbox in multiple mode, check in single mode. |
| `chips` | `boolean` | `false` | Multiple mode: render selected items as removable chips in the trigger instead of a count. |
| `maxVisibleChips` | `number` | `3` | Number of chips shown before collapsing the remainder into "+N". |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `"Select…"` | Trigger text when nothing is selected; also the listbox accessible name. |
| `searchPlaceholder` | `string` | `"Search…"` | Placeholder for the search input. |
| `emptyMessage` | `string` | `"No options found"` | Shown when search yields no matches. |
| `selectAllLabel` | `string` | `"Select all"` | Label for the select-all row (switches to "Deselect all" when all are selected). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disable the whole control. |
| `theme` | `"light" \| "dark"` | `"dark"` | Theme for default trigger and panel colors. |
| `className` | `string` | — | Additional classes merged onto the root wrapper. |

### Usage

```tsx
"use client";
import { Dropdown } from "@/components/ui/dropdown";
import { Shield, Settings, User, Globe } from "lucide-react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="flex h-[440px] w-full justify-center px-6 pt-10">
      <Dropdown
        theme="dark"
        placeholder="Select a role"
        clearable
        options={[
          { value: "admin", label: "Administrator", icon: <Shield className="h-4 w-4 text-purple-400" />, description: "Full access to everything" },
          { value: "editor", label: "Editor", icon: <Settings className="h-4 w-4 text-blue-400" />, description: "Can create and edit content" },
          { value: "viewer", label: "Viewer", icon: <User className="h-4 w-4 text-green-400" />, description: "Read-only access" },
          { value: "guest", label: "Guest", icon: <Globe className="h-4 w-4 text-neutral-400" />, disabled: true },
        ]}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Scenario: Single select with icons and descriptions

A role picker where each option carries an icon and a helper line, one entry is disabled, and the selection can be cleared.

```tsx
"use client";
import { Dropdown } from "@/components/ui/dropdown";
import { Shield, Settings, User } from "lucide-react";

export default function RolePicker() {
  return (
    <Dropdown
      placeholder="Select a role"
      clearable
      onChange={(v) => console.log(v)}
      options={[
        { value: "admin", label: "Administrator", icon: <Shield className="h-4 w-4" />, description: "Full access" },
        { value: "editor", label: "Editor", icon: <Settings className="h-4 w-4" />, description: "Edit content" },
        { value: "viewer", label: "Viewer", icon: <User className="h-4 w-4" />, description: "Read only" },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

### Scenario: Multi-select with search, select all and chips

Pick many values with a filter box, a Select all / Deselect all toggle, removable chips in the trigger, and color dots per option.

```tsx
"use client";
import { useState } from "react";
import { Dropdown } from "@/components/ui/dropdown";

export default function TechPicker() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<string[]>(["react"]);
  return (
    <Dropdown
      multiple
      searchable
      clearable
      showSelectAll
      chips
      value={value}
      onChange={(v) => setValue(v as string[])}
      placeholder="Pick technologies"
      options={[
        { value: "react", label: "React", color: "#61dafb" },
        { value: "vue", label: "Vue", color: "#42b883" },
        { value: "svelte", label: "Svelte", color: "#ff3e00" },
        { value: "ts", label: "TypeScript", color: "#3178c6" },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

### Scenario: Grouped options with radio indicators

Single-choice plan selector where options are grouped into sections and marked with radio buttons.

```tsx
"use client";
import { Dropdown } from "@/components/ui/dropdown";

        { value: "enterprise", label: "Enterprise", description: "Contact us", group: "Teams" },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

### Scenario: Count display, clearable, with disabled options

Multi-select that shows an "N selected" count instead of chips, can be cleared in one click, and skips disabled options during selection and keyboard navigation. Set `disabled` on the component to lock the whole control.

```tsx
"use client";
import { Dropdown } from "@/components/ui/dropdown";

export default function PermissionPicker() {
  return (
    <Dropdown
      multiple
      searchable
      clearable
      showSelectAll
      defaultValue={["read"]}
      placeholder="Select permissions"
      options={[
        { value: "read", label: "Read", color: "#22c55e" },
        { value: "write", label: "Write", color: "#eab308" },
        { value: "delete", label: "Delete", color: "#ef4444" },
        { value: "admin", label: "Admin", color: "#a855f7", disabled: true },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```
